newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds cool off after blistering week.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds cool off after blistering week.

text.p: *Australian bond yields ended higher as the market booked profits and squared up after this week's strong rally, unable to push on the move in the absence of a policy easing.
*Rate cut now seen more likely after August board meeting.
Australian bond yields ended higher as the market booked profits and squared up after this week's strong rally, unable to push on the move in the absence of a monetary policy easing.

The market is still largely pricing in a 50 basis point easing in current 5.5 official interest rates, although with the Reserve Bank remaining quiet on policy today, analysts now think such a move is more likely after the August 5 board meeting.
Ten-year bond yields fell below 6.4 percent on Thursday and their lowest level since the early 1980s after this week's inflation and wages data was seen clinching a rate cut.
September bill futures also eased to 93.93, but still equated to a cash rate of 5.07 percent and well below the current level of official rates.
Analysts also doubt that next week's data for retail trade and building approvals will change the easing possibility.

Median forecasts centre on a 1.5 percent fall for Wednesday's June building approvals and a rise of just 0.4 percent for retail trade for the same month on Thursday, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

The market's weaker tone saw spreads give up some ground to the dollar bloc after Thursday's tightening. The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread made a strong test of 25 basis points on Thursday, its lowest level since the early 1980s. New Zealand bonds were supported by bounce in the N.Z. TWI.
